title: Could This Samsung Flip8 Be Your Last Chance to Snag a Small Foldable Smartphone?
gist: WIRED rates Samsung's $1,200 Galaxy Z Flip8 7/10. It is the slimmest and lightest flip phone, with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and seven years of updates, but it is a minor upgrade over the Z Flip7 at a $100 higher price. Battery life, charging and the cover screen remain weak points. Persistent rumors say Samsung may retire the flip format as the Fold8 competes with the iPhone Duo, which leaves Motorola's Razr as the only rival.

themes.theme: Incremental upgrade at a higher price

insights.claim: Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip8 costs $100 more than the Z Flip7 while offering only tiny improvements. It is 0.55 mm slimmer and 8 g lighter, with a newer processor and an improved hinge, and the screens are unchanged.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Smartphone makers are raising prices without meaningful hardware gains, which weakens the case for upgrading.
insights.quote: Like almost every other phone this year, the Z Flip8 offers tiny improvements over its predecessor and costs $100 more.
insights.locator: Like almost every other phone this year

insights.claim: The Galaxy Z Flip8 uses the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy, the same chip as Samsung's larger foldables, with 12 GB RAM and 256 GB storage. Moving to 512 GB costs $200 more.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Qualcomm's flagship chip is now used across Samsung's whole foldable lineup.
insights.locator: Flip phones used to get palmed off

insights.claim: The Galaxy Z Flip8 has average battery life from a 4,300-mAh silicon-carbon cell and slow 25 W wired and 15 W wireless charging. It does not support Qi2 magnetic charging or UWB, which the Fold8 models have.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Battery is a lasting limit of the compact form factor and a reason buyers pick rivals.
insights.locator: While it’s very capable, the Z Flip8

insights.claim: Samsung's new AI features on the Z Flip8 include My FanCam, which reframes group videos around a chosen subject, Now Brief for surfacing calendar events and information, and Now Nudge for contextual suggestions such as adding dates from messages.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: On-device AI features are now the main way Android flagships set themselves apart.
insights.locator: Another new AI feature from Samsung

insights.claim: Running most third-party apps on the Z Flip8's FlexWindow cover screen still requires installing Good Lock and the MultiStar plug-in. Meanwhile, Samsung preinstalls third-party bloatware such as Facebook, Spotify and Instagram.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Preinstall deals bring Samsung revenue but hurt the experience on premium devices.
insights.quote: it's disgraceful that Samsung is including bloatware on a phone this expensive

insights.claim: The Galaxy Z Flip8 gets seven years of platform and security updates, which could keep it supported until 2033.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Long support windows lengthen replacement cycles, which slows hardware upgrade revenue.
insights.locator: Sadly, this might be your last chance

insights.claim: Persistent rumors suggest Samsung will retire the flip-phone form factor as the Galaxy Z Fold8 takes off and competes head-to-head with the iPhone Duo. Samsung has not confirmed this.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: This would mean consolidation toward book-style foldables driven by Apple's entry into the category.
insights.quote: Persistent rumors suggest Samsung will sunset this form factor as the Fold8 takes off and goes head-to-head with the iPhone Duo
insights.locator: Sadly, this might be your last chance

insights.claim: Motorola's Razr line is Samsung's only real flip-phone competitor. The Razr costs $800, the Razr+ $1,100 with an older processor and shorter support, and the Razr Ultra $1,500 with a better camera, more memory and faster charging.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: If Samsung exits, Motorola could have the flip-phone niche almost to itself.

insights.claim: WIRED rates the Galaxy Z Flip8 7/10. It calls the flip format arguably the most practical type of folding phone, but says Z Flip7 owners should not upgrade.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Weak reasons to upgrade point to soft replacement demand within the installed base.
insights.locator: Like almost every other phone this year
